title: tc-help-video
description: Point-in-time help: a small film-frame icon to put beside a heading or label, opening one short tutorial in a modal player with captions and chapters.

heading.description: The video's title – the tooltip, the player's heading and the icon's accessible name

description.description: A line or two about what it shows, under the player

duration.description: Its length in seconds, shown in the tooltip and the player

src.description: A video file the browser can play

type.description: The file's type, e.g. "video/mp4", when the URL doesn't say

poster.description: The player's picture before it plays

embed.description: An embed URL from a video host, played in an iframe instead of `src`

chapters.description: Points in the video to jump to (with `src`)

label.description: Words beside the icon, e.g. "Watch how"; unset, the icon stands alone with a tooltip

size.description: The icon's size against the text around it: "sm" (1em), "md" (1.25em, the default) or "lg" (1.5em)

watched.description: Whether it has been watched – a check on the icon. Set when a file plays to its end, unless a tc-watched-change listener calls preventDefault()

open.description: Whether the player is open. Changed by the user unless a tc-open-change listener calls preventDefault()

autoplay.description: Start playing a file as soon as the player opens

transcript.description: The transcript's lines, `{ time, text }`. Unset, it's read from the `captions` file when first shown

transcriptFile.description: A transcript file to download instead of the text one made from the lines, e.g. a PDF

updatedOn.description: When the video last changed, as a date ("2026-11-12"); for `new-days` days after it, a dot on the icon says so

newDays.description: How many days after `updated-on` the dot shows (default 14)

updateSeen.description: Whether this person has seen the update – the dot is cleared. Set when the player opens, unless a tc-update-seen-change listener calls preventDefault()

now.description: The time to measure `new-days` from, in milliseconds; unset, the clock's
